top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock is a distinct invention (many-atom, Doppler- and recoil-free, light shift cancelled) from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. Its 10^-18 realisation, including the resolved gravitational redshift across a millimetre sample, is reproduced across independent laboratories with every systematic traceable to a physical effect. A two-name Katori-Ye allocation with a concept-plus-realisation citation is defensible; the priority record against Ludlow, Lemonde and Hinkley is an open point I would want checked by an outside report. P003 follows as the most mature of the other proposals, though its credit boundary (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) is untidy. P002 comes next since the field is only about eight years old and the pairing mechanism is open. An award is still preferred to no award.
recusal_note: Year in John Hall's JILA laboratory during my PhD; no collaboration with Katori or Ye, so no apparent recusal need. Otherwise none apparent from profile.
